parts.title: Part 1

passage.title: Television
passage.content:
The effects of _____(1)_____ have been much debated since it became widely available in the 1950s. There is little doubt that watching it has significant effects on _____(2)_____. Modern television is found in nearly every home, and many people consider it one of the most influential inventions of the twentieth century.

Those who are most influenced by TV are _____(3)_____. This is mainly because the amount of time they spend watching it is huge. For example, in the United States, children watch between three and four hours per day. They will have watched 8,000 hours before they even start school. By the time they are 18, they will have spent more time watching TV than any other single activity apart from sleeping.

A concern that is often raised is the question of _____(4)_____ on TV. Researches have established that children who watch TV are more likely to behave aggressively. Many studies show that exposure to violence in fictional shows can desensitise young viewers over time. Their _____(5)_____ can help limit the effects of what they see, however. Responsible parents often set firm rules about what their children can watch and how long they spend in front of the screen each day.

On the positive side, TV has the power to teach. Many educational _____(6)_____ help children learn about the world, widen their vocabulary, and develop numeracy. Documentaries, news bulletins and well-designed children's programs are common examples of broadcasts that combine entertainment with genuine learning.

parts.instruction: Read the text about television. Choose the best word from the box for each gap. There are two extra words you do not need.

q1.text: The passage discusses the effects of a media device that became popular in the 1950s. The text repeatedly uses the abbreviation 'TV' and the verb 'watching,' confirming the subject. That's why the correct answer is 'television'.
q1.quote: By the time they are 18, they will have spent more time watching TV than any other single activity apart from sleeping.

q2.text: The sentence introduces the general idea that watching TV affects viewers. The following sentences then specify which groups, like children, are most influenced, implying a broader group was mentioned first. That's why the correct answer is 'people'.

q3.text: The passage states that a certain group is most influenced by TV. The very next sentence gives an example of this group, mentioning how much time they spend watching television. That's why the correct answer is 'children'.
q3.quote: For example, in the United States, children watch between three and four hours per day.

q4.text: The passage raises a concern about TV content. The next sentence explains this concern by linking TV watching to aggressive behavior, which is a direct consequence of viewing violent content. That's why the correct answer is 'violence'.
q4.quote: Researches have established that children who watch TV are more likely to behave aggressively.

q5.text: The sentence discusses who can limit the negative effects of TV on children. In this context, the most logical answer is the adults responsible for the children, as suggested by the hint 'mothers and fathers'. That's why the correct answer is 'parents'.

q6.text: The sentence describes the positive, educational content available on TV. The specific term for individual shows or series on television that can teach children is 'programs', as indicated by the hint 'TV shows'. That's why the correct answer is 'programs'.

statements.text: PARADOX CHRONICLES. Venture into the unknown with this captivating sci-fi series that explores alternate realities, time travel, and the very nature of existence. With an engrossing storyline and a diverse cast of characters, Paradox Chronicles will keep you on the edge of your seat, questioning the fabric of reality itself.

YORKMAN. In this movie, one detective, when trying to solve a mystery, gets bitten by a radioactive fish and he transforms into a fish people king called 'Yorkman'. Suitable for both young and old audience who wants to watch superhero flick adventure.

FATE'S DESIGN. A thought-provoking drama series that delves into the lives of interconnected strangers, exploring themes of destiny, love, and the choices that shape our lives. Perfect for those who appreciate deep storytelling and character development.

ADVENTURES OF SMARTY AND FRIENDS. Join Smarty the owl and his friends on exciting adventures that teach valuable lessons about friendship, problem-solving, and the world around us. A fun and educational cartoon perfect for young children.

WAR ECHOES. A gripping documentary series that takes viewers through the pivotal moments of World War II, featuring rare footage and firsthand accounts from veterans. A must-watch for history enthusiasts.

SHADOW'S PURSUIT. Follow Detective Sarah Cole as she navigates the dark underbelly of the city, solving complex crimes and uncovering shocking truths. A thrilling mystery series with unexpected plot twists.
WARTALES. An animated series for adolescents featuring space adventures. Not suitable for children under 10.

LIFE ON CAMPUS. A hilarious sitcom that follows the misadventures of a group of college students as they navigate classes, relationships, and the ups and downs of university life. Perfect for unwinding after a long day.

WONDERS OF THE WILD. Immerse yourself in the breathtaking beauty of nature with this stunning documentary series. From the depths of the ocean to the peaks of mountains, explore the wonders of the natural world.

CULINARY FRONTIERS. Join renowned chef Marco as he travels the globe, discovering unique cuisines and learning traditional cooking techniques from local experts. A feast for the eyes and the taste buds.

parts.title: Part 3

paragraphs.content: English is spoken as a first language by about 375 million people and as a second language by around 375 million more. It is the official or semi-official language in over 60 countries and is prominent in over 20 more. It is the dominant language on the Internet and in international business, science, and aviation.

English developed from the languages of Germanic tribes (Angles, Saxons, and Jutes) who settled in Britain from the 5th century. The name 'English' comes from 'Angles,' one of these tribes. The language was influenced by Norse invaders in the 8th and 9th centuries and later by the Norman Conquest of 1066.

One notable feature of English is the large number of words it has borrowed from other languages. About 80% of English vocabulary is foreign in origin. Words have been adopted from Latin, French, Greek, and many other languages.

Although British English and American English are generally similar, there are differences in spelling (colour/color), vocabulary (lift/elevator), and pronunciation. Australian, Indian, and other varieties of English also have their distinctive features.

English has become the global language of communication. More people learn English as a foreign language than any other. It is estimated that about one billion people are currently learning English worldwide.

Many language learners find that watching English films, listening to English songs, and reading English books are effective ways to improve their skills. Immersion in the language through travel or living abroad is also popular.

parts.title: Part 4

passage.title: Nostradamus the Prophet
passage.content:
Michel de Nostredame, better known as Nostradamus, was born in Saint-Remy-de-Provence, France, in December 1503. He became famous for his book of prophecies, first published in 1555, which many believe predicted future events.

Nostradamus initially trained as a physician and gained a reputation for treating plague victims. However, he became interested in the occult and began making predictions. His prophecies were written in quatrains - four-line verses - and grouped into sets of 100 called "centuries."

The prophecies are deliberately vague and written in a mixture of languages including French, Greek, and Latin. This makes them open to many interpretations. Supporters claim he predicted events such as the Great Fire of London, the French Revolution, Napoleon's rise, both World Wars, and the September 11 attacks.

Critics argue that his writings are so ambiguous that they can be fitted to almost any event after it has happened. Scientific analysis has found no evidence that his success rate is any better than chance. Despite this, his books have rarely been out of print and continue to attract interest, especially during times of crisis or at the turn of centuries.

Nostradamus died on July 2, 1566. According to legend, he predicted his own death, telling his secretary the night before: "You will not find me alive at sunrise." Whether this is true or just another myth surrounding this enigmatic figure remains uncertain.

parts.title: Part 5

passage.title: Malaria in Italy
passage.content:
Malaria was once a major health problem in Italy, particularly in the southern regions and areas with marshlands. The disease was spread by insects that bred in stagnant water, and it affected millions of Italians over the centuries.

The name "malaria" itself comes from Italian, meaning "bad air" - people originally believed the disease was caused by the unclean air from swamps rather than by insects. This misconception persisted for centuries until scientists discovered the true cause.

In the early 20th century, Italy launched a major campaign to eradicate malaria. This involved draining marshes, distributing quinine (an anti-malarial drug), and using insecticides. The campaign was remarkably successful, and by 1970, Italy was declared malaria-free by the World Health Organization.

Before eradication, malaria had a profound impact on Italian society. It caused high mortality rates, particularly among children, and left survivors weakened and unable to work effectively. The disease seemed to run in families, leading some to believe it was hereditary. Entire regions were affected, and the disease was a major factor in the poverty of southern Italy.

The conquest of malaria in Italy led to significant improvements in health and life expectancy. Areas that were once avoided because of the disease became habitable and productive. This transformation contributed to Italy's economic development in the latter half of the 20th century.

parts.instruction: Read the following text for questions 30-35.

q30.text: The passage explicitly states that the disease was transmitted by small creatures that bred in stagnant water, which is found in marshes. That's why the correct answer is 'insects'.
q30.quote: The disease was spread by insects that bred in stagnant water, and it affected millions of Italians over the centuries.

q31.text: The text explains that people originally thought the disease came from the 'bad air' from swamps. The word 'unclean' is a synonym for 'bad' in this context. That's why the correct answer is 'unclean'.

q32.text: The passage directly states that because the disease often affected multiple people in the same family, some people believed it was passed down genetically. That's why the correct answer is 'hereditary'.
q32.quote: The disease seemed to run in families, leading some to believe it was hereditary.

q33.text: The passage lists the positive results of conquering malaria, explicitly mentioning that the average length of a person's life improved significantly. That's why the correct answer is 'expectancy'.
q33.quote: The conquest of malaria in Italy led to significant improvements in health and life expectancy.

q34.text: The passage lists the methods used in the campaign: draining marshes, distributing medicine, and using insecticides. Vaccinating the population is not mentioned as part of the effort. That's why the correct answer is A.
q34.quote: This involved draining marshes, distributing quinine (an anti-malarial drug), and using insecticides.

q35.text: The passage concludes by stating that making areas habitable and productive after eliminating malaria directly contributed to the country's economic progress. That's why the correct answer is D.
q35.quote: This transformation contributed to Italy's economic development in the latter half of the 20th century.
